message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm an AITA (Asshole in This Argument) for wanting to back out of the promise I made to my wife. Let me start by understanding the situation. I cheated on my wife, which is a big deal. I owned up to it, and she gave me a chance to make things right by agreeing to make the next year all about her. I thought that meant doing things like massages, shopping, and other things she likes. But instead, she decided the year should be all about Disney. I didn't realize she was that into Disney. Our daughters loved it when they were little, but now they're out of the house. I assumed her interest was mostly for the kids. But she's made me go to Disneyland seven times this year and Harry Potter World once. I went along because I thought it was part of making things right, but it's getting expensive and exhausting. She even made me cosplay as Disney characters, including a Beauty and the Beast costume that cost $800. Now, she's making me watch Frozen every day, and when I asked to change it, she put on Pocahontas 2. I know this isn't as bad as her being cheated on, but I'm really miserable and can't keep doing this. I want to have an intervention where we stop all the Disney stuff and just go to counseling, which we should have done a while ago. Am I an asshole for wanting to back out? Let me think about this. First, I cheated, which is a huge betrayal. My wife gave me a chance to fix things, and I agreed to make the year about her. But I didn't realize what that meant. She chose Disney, which is a big part of her life now, even though I didn't see it before. I went along with it, but it's taking a toll on me financially and emotionally. I'm spending a lot of money on trips and costumes, and I'm not happy about it. I feel like I'm not getting the support I need because we haven't gone to counseling yet. I want to stop the Disney stuff and focus on counseling because I think that's more important for our relationship. But is that fair? Did I make a promise that I should keep, even if it's making me unhappy? Or is it reasonable to want to change the approach since it's not working for me? I also need to consider her feelings. She might feel like I'm not keeping my promise, which could hurt her again. But I'm also in pain and need help. Maybe we need to communicate better and find a middle ground where both of us can feel heard and supported. I'm not sure if wanting to back out makes me an asshole. It's a tough situation because I want to fix things, but I'm not sure how to do it without causing more pain. Maybe I should talk to her about how I'm feeling and see if we can adjust our plan together.
